themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens spiked to 29 THIS WEEK, a 132% jump from the 8-week baseline average of 12.5 complaints per week (z-score: 3.84), suggesting new or intensified commercial activity or enforcement gaps affecting residential quality of life.
evidence: 29 commercial noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.84 indicates statistically significant spike
132% increase suggests sudden change, not gradual escalation
reporting_angles: Interview residents on specific blocks experiencing commercial noise; identify which businesses are generating complaints
Check 311 complaint locations to map geographic clustering; identify if spike correlates with new restaurant/bar openings or construction

themes_detail.label: Dead Trees & Park Decline
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK, a 233% spike from the 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.04), suggesting possible storm damage, disease, or neglected maintenance affecting neighborhood greenspace and aligning with community board requests for park upgrades.
evidence: 5 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly baseline average
Z-score of 4.04 indicates high statistical significance
Aligns with recurring community board budget requests to 'reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity' and 'enhance park safety'
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent weather events (heavy winds, ice) damaged trees across specific parks (Prospect Park boundary, neighborhood green spaces)
Document Parks Department response time; cross-reference with maintenance budget and staffing

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints exploded to 3 LAST WEEK, a 2300% spike from the 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.69, highest severity), paired with vendor enforcement complaints up 700%, suggesting unregulated or rapidly expanding street vending creating public space conflicts.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% increase)
5 vendor enforcement complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% increase)
Z-score of 8.69 represents the single largest statistical anomaly in dataset
reporting_angles: Identify which blocks or intersections are seeing new food vendor activity; interview residents and business owners about complaints
Check if vendor complaints correlate with Parks Department enforcement actions or licensing changes; speak to Dept. of Consumer Affairs

themes_detail.label: Curb & Street Obstruction Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints spiked to 37 TWO WEEKS AGO (492% above baseline of 6.2/week, z-score: 7.26), and obstruction complaints hit 15 (275% above 4.0/week baseline, z-score: 5.5), suggesting systematic street-level maintenance failures or construction debris affecting pedestrian access.
evidence: 37 curb condition complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 6.2 weekly baseline (492% increase, z-score: 7.26)
15 obstruction complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 4.0 weekly baseline (275% increase, z-score: 5.5)
Combined signal indicates widespread street-level infrastructure or maintenance issue
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify geographic hotspots; document what specific curb/street conditions residents are reporting (potholes, debris, illegally parked vehicles)
Check DOB permit data (1,233 total filings, 787 alterations) to determine if construction activity is generating debris; verify Sanitation Department street-cleaning frequency

themes_detail.label: Water System & Infrastructure Stress
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints remain in top 10 (351 over 90 days), and community board repeatedly requests water main inspection/repair for specific street segments, signaling long-running infrastructure vulnerability that may be exacerbated by recent street condition spikes.
evidence: Water system complaints: 351 over 90 days (rank 9 out of top issues)
Heat/hot water complaints: 912 over 90 days (rank 2), indicating potential water-system heating failures
Community board budget requests repeatedly cite 'inspect water main on specific street segment' (unfunded, recurring request)
reporting_angles: Identify which street segments are mentioned in community board water main requests; file FOIL requests for DEP water break history and maintenance backlogs
Interview residents about service reliability; cross-reference heat/hot water complaints (912 total) with water system infrastructure age in district
